title: MPAPASS - Gating Flow Cytometry Multiplex Data
author: Joshua A Welsh
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bjnwkmfe
materials: In preparation for the MPAPASS software, you will have to manually rename the 99 bead population from the export suffix of 89_99_99.csv to simply _99.csv Repeat if this occurs with the 89 bead population.

steps.title: Import Samples into FlowJo
steps.instruction: Import the desired files into the FlowJo workspace using the 'Add Samples' button under the FlowJo tab or by dragging files into the software.

substeps.instruction: Calibrate fluorescence parameters into standard units of 'molecules of equivalent soluble fluorophore' (MESF) using FCMPASS software and commercially available MESF beads for reproducibility.

steps.title: Gate for Singlets
steps.instruction: Open a scatter plot by double-clicking a sample (e.g., A1.fcs) and gate for single events.

substeps.instruction: Set scatter plot parameters to FSC-A and SSC-A channels.
Apply a rectangular gate around the single events.

steps.title: Identify and Gate Bead Populations
steps.instruction: Open the gated Singlets population in a new scatter plot to identify the bead populations.

substeps.instruction: Set parameters to FITC-A and PE-A channels.
Use elliptical gates to isolate each of the 39 distinct bead populations based on the bead legend.
For the merged 89 and 99 bead populations, gate around the entire merged population for later separation.

steps.title: Separate Merged Populations 89 and 99
steps.instruction: If populations 89 and 99 are not adequately separated, create a derived parameter to distinguish them.

substeps.instruction: Select the sample used for gating (e.g., A1.fcs), navigate to the Tools tab, and click 'Derive Parameters'.
Name the derived parameter '89,99 Sep'.
Use the 'Insert Reference' button to select the V-525-A channel, click the division button, and then use 'Insert Reference' to select the V-660-A channel.
In the Scale tab, select 'Linear' scale and set Min to 0 and Max to 10, then click OK.

steps.title: Resolve Merged Population Gating
steps.instruction: Use the derived parameter to split the merged 89_99 subpopulation.

substeps.instruction: Open the 89_99 subpopulation in a new scatter plot.
Set the X-axis to the '89,99 Sep' derived parameter and the Y-axis to the histogram option.
Use the Bisector Tool to gate the two populations at a point of distinct separation.
Right-click to relabel the upper population as '99' and the lower population as '89'.

steps.title: Apply Gating to All Samples
steps.instruction: Apply the established gating hierarchy to all files in the workspace.

substeps.instruction: Highlight all gated populations and the derived parameter in the FlowJo workspace.
Drag these selections into the 'All Samples Group' to apply the gates to all samples.

steps.title: Export Data to CSV
steps.instruction: Export the gated population data into .csv files.

substeps.instruction: Select all bead populations for one sample, then under the Edit tab, click 'Select Equivalent Nodes' to select the same populations across all samples.
Navigate to the File tab and click 'Export/Concatenate Populations'.
Set the format to 'CSV - Scale Values'.
Uncheck 'Include Header'.
Set the destination folder.
Click 'Custom Set of Parameters', then 'View/Edit', and choose the 'APC' parameter from the list.
Click 'Export' to generate the files.
